overview: Mentions of the Auditor-General in the NSW Parliament between November 2025 and October 2026 mixed members citing audit findings in debate with the Clerk announcing reports received. The main threads were the Regional Roads Fund report, train fleet procurement, the Resilient Homes and Lands Programs and the Fines Legislation Amendment Bill; the Public Accounts Committee also reported on the Audit Office's 2026-27 appropriation. Members also drew on findings about Aboriginal land claims, consultants and grants administration.

issues.label: Regional Roads Fund report and call for papers
issues.note: Members cited the Auditor-General's May 2026 report on projects moved from the Urban Roads Fund without documented rationale; papers were sought, the Government declined.

issues.label: Rail fleet procurement report used in debate
issues.note: Members repeatedly cited Auditor-General findings on regional and intercity train procurement, including a $2.5 billion blowout, in arguments about the former government's record.

issues.label: Resilient Homes and Lands audit questions
issues.note: Members cited the May 2026 audit of the $980 million Resilient programs, including claims of no homes delivered and no business case.

issues.label: Audit Office funding and Public Accounts Committee
issues.note: Public Accounts Committee inquired into and reported on the Auditor-General's 2026-27 appropriation, noting one performance audit funding proposal was approved below the amount sought.

issues.label: Fines bill and Revenue NSW hardship review
issues.note: Fines Legislation Amendment Bill debate drew on the October 2025 review of Revenue NSW hardship assistance, including the Hardship Review Board's independence.

issues.label: Auditor-General powers and requests for new audits
issues.note: 'Follow the dollar' powers were compared with ICAC's jurisdiction, and members sought or welcomed audits of Concord Hospital, ambulance recruitment, grants and firearms administration.

debates.gist: Non-government members cited the Auditor-General's 6 May 2026 Regional Roads Fund report, including undocumented project transfers and incomplete business cases, in support of a call for papers; the Government opposed it, saying the Auditor-General had already examined the matters.

Second reading debate on the Fines Legislation Amendment Bill 2025. Speakers referred to the Auditor-General's review of Revenue NSW hardship assistance, including the Hardship Review Board's independence; the Minister said reforms were under way in parallel.
